verses.zh: 耶路・巴力的儿子亚比米勒到了示剑见他的众母舅，对他们和他外祖全家的人说：
verses.en: Now Abimelech son of Jerub Baal[NOTE:1] went to Shechem to see his mother’s relatives.[NOTE:2] He said to them and to his mother’s entire extended family,[NOTE:3]
notes: That is, Gideon, and so throughout Judges 9. Gideon was given the name Jerub Baal (meaning “Let Baal fight”) in Judges 6:32.
Heb “brothers.”
Heb “to all the extended family of the house of the father of his mother.”

verses.zh: 「请你们问示剑的众人说，是耶路・巴力的众子七十人都管理你们好呢？还是一人管理你们好呢？你们又要记念我是你们的骨肉。」
verses.en: “Tell[NOTE:1] all the leaders of Shechem this: ‘Why would you want[NOTE:2] to have 70 men, all Jerub Baal’s sons, ruling over you when you can have just one ruler? Recall that I am your own flesh and blood.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Speak into the ears of.”
Heb “What good is it to you?”
Heb “your bone and your flesh.”

verses.zh: 他的众母舅便将这一切话为他说给示剑人听，示剑人的心就归向亚比米勒。他们说：「他原是我们的弟兄」；
verses.en: His mother’s relatives[NOTE:1] spoke on his behalf to[NOTE:2] all the leaders of Shechem and reported his proposal.[NOTE:3] The leaders were drawn to Abimelech;[NOTE:4] they said, “He is our close relative.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “brothers.”
Heb “into the ears of.”
Heb “and all these words.”
Heb “Their heart was inclined after Abimelech.”
Heb “our brother.”

verses.zh: 就从巴力・比利土的庙中取了七十舍客勒银子给亚比米勒；亚比米勒用以雇了些匪徒跟随他。
verses.en: They paid him 70 silver shekels out of the temple of Baal Berith. Abimelech then used the silver to hire some lawless, dangerous[NOTE:1] men as his followers.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “empty and reckless.”
Heb “and they followed him.”

verses.zh: 他往俄弗拉到他父亲的家，将他弟兄、耶路・巴力的众子七十人都杀在一块磐石上；只剩下耶路・巴力的小儿子约坦，因为他躲藏了。
verses.en: He went to his father’s home in Ophrah and murdered his half brothers,[NOTE:1] the 70 legitimate[NOTE:2] sons of Jerub Baal, on one stone. Only Jotham, Jerub Baal’s youngest son, escaped,[NOTE:3] because he hid.
notes: Heb “his brothers.”
The word “legitimate” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “remained.”

verses.zh: 示剑人和米罗人都一同聚集，往示剑橡树旁的柱子那里，立亚比米勒为王。
verses.en: All the leaders of Shechem and Beth Millo assembled and then went and made Abimelech king by the oak near the pillar[NOTE:1] in Shechem.
notes: The translation assumes that the form in the Hebrew text (מֻצָּב, mutsav) should be מַצֵּבָה (matsevah, “pillar”). The reference is probably to a pagan object of worship (cf. LXX).

verses.zh: 有人将这事告诉约坦，他就去站在基利心山顶上，向众人大声喊叫说：「示剑人哪，你们要听我的话，　神也就听你们的话。
verses.en: When Jotham heard the news,[NOTE:1] he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim. He spoke loudly to the people below,[NOTE:2] “Listen to me, leaders of Shechem, so that God may listen to you!
notes: Heb “And they reported to Jotham.” The subject of the plural verb is indefinite.
Heb “He lifted his voice and called and said to them.”

verses.zh: 有一时，树木要膏一树为王，管理他们，就去对橄榄树说：『请你作我们的王。』
verses.en: “The trees were determined to go out[NOTE:1] and choose a king for themselves.[NOTE:2] They said to the olive tree, ‘Be our king!’[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Going they went, the trees.” The precise emphatic force of the infinitive absolute (“Going”) is not entirely clear. Perhaps here it indicates determination, as in Gen 31:30, where one might translate, “You have insisted on going away.”
Heb “to anoint [with oil] over them a king.”
Or “Rule over us!”

verses.zh: 橄榄树回答说：『我岂肯止住供奉神和尊重人的油，飘颻在众树之上呢？』
verses.en: But the olive tree said to them, ‘I am not going to stop producing my oil, which is used to honor gods and men, just to sway above the other trees!’[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Should I stop my abundance, with which they honor gods and men, and go to sway over the trees?” The negative sentence in the translation reflects the force of the rhetorical question.

verses.zh: 树木对无花果树说：『请你来作我们的王。』
verses.en: “So the trees said to the fig tree, ‘You come and be our king!’[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “and rule over us!”

verses.zh: 无花果树回答说：『我岂肯止住所结甜美的果子，飘颻在众树之上呢？』
verses.en: But the fig tree said to them, ‘I am not going to stop producing my sweet figs, my excellent fruit, just to sway above the other trees!’[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Should I stop my sweetness and my good fruit and go to sway over the trees?” The negative sentence in the translation reflects the force of the rhetorical question.

verses.zh: 树木对葡萄树说：『请你来作我们的王。』
verses.en: “So the trees said to the grapevine, ‘You come and be our king!’[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “and rule over us!”

verses.zh: 葡萄树回答说：『我岂肯止住使神和人喜乐的新酒，飘颻在众树之上呢。』
verses.en: But the grapevine said to them, ‘I am not going to stop producing my wine, which makes gods and men so happy, just to sway above the other trees!’[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Should I stop my wine, which makes happy gods and men, and go to sway over the trees?” The negative sentence in the translation reflects the force of the rhetorical question.

verses.zh: 众树对荆棘说：『请你来作我们的王。』
verses.en: “So all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘You come and be our king!’[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “and rule over us!”

verses.zh: 荆棘回答说：『你们若诚诚实实地膏我为王，就要投在我的荫下；不然，愿火从荆棘里出来，烧灭黎巴嫩的香柏树。』
verses.en: The thornbush said to the trees, ‘If you really want to choose[NOTE:1] me as your king, then come along, find safety under my branches.[NOTE:2] Otherwise[NOTE:3] may fire blaze from the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon!’
notes: Heb “are about to anoint [with oil].”
Heb “in my shade.”
Heb “If not.”

verses.zh: 「现在你们立亚比米勒为王，若按诚实正直善待耶路・巴力和他的全家，这就是酬他的劳。
verses.en: “Now, if you have shown loyalty and integrity when you made Abimelech king, if you have done right to Jerub Baal and his family,[NOTE:1] if you have properly repaid him[NOTE:2]—
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “if according to the deeds of his hands you have done to him.”

verses.zh: 从前我父冒死为你们争战，救了你们脱离米甸人的手。
verses.en: my father fought for you; he risked his life[NOTE:1] and delivered you from Midian’s power.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “threw his life out in front,” that is, “exposed himself to danger.” The MT form מִנֶּגֶד (minneged, “from before”) should probably be read as מִנֶּגְדּוֹ (minnegdo, “from before him”); haplography of vav has likely occurred here in the MT.
Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 你们如今起来攻击我的父家，将他众子七十人杀在一块磐石上，又立他婢女所生的儿子亚比米勒为示剑人的王；他原是你们的弟兄。
verses.en: But you have attacked[NOTE:1] my father’s family[NOTE:2] today. You murdered his 70 legitimate[NOTE:3] sons on one stone and made Abimelech, the son of his female slave, king over the leaders of Shechem just because he is your close relative.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “have risen up against.”
Heb “house.”
The word “legitimate” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “your brother.”

verses.zh: 你们如今若按诚实正直待耶路・巴力和他的家，就可因亚比米勒得欢乐，他也可因你们得欢乐；
verses.en: So if you have shown loyalty and integrity to Jerub Baal and his family[NOTE:1] today, then may Abimelech bring you happiness and may you bring him happiness![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “then rejoice in Abimelech, and may he also rejoice in you.”

verses.zh: 不然，愿火从亚比米勒发出，烧灭示剑人和米罗众人，又愿火从示剑人和米罗人中出来，烧灭亚比米勒。」
verses.en: But if not, may fire blaze from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth Millo! May fire also blaze from the leaders of Shechem and Beth Millo and consume Abimelech!”

verses.zh: 约坦因怕他弟兄亚比米勒，就逃跑，来到比珥，住在那里。
verses.en: Then Jotham ran away[NOTE:1] to Beer and lived there to escape from[NOTE:2] Abimelech his half-brother.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “fled and ran away and went.”
Heb “there from before.”
Heb “his brother.”

verses.zh: 亚比米勒管理以色列人三年。
verses.en: Abimelech commanded[NOTE:1] Israel for three years.
notes: The Hebrew verb translated “commanded” (שָׂרַר, sarar), which appears only here in Judges, differs from the ones employed earlier in this chapter (מָשַׁל [mashal] and מָלַךְ [malakh]).sn Abimelech commanded Israel. Perhaps while ruling as king over the city-state of Shechem, Abimelech also became a leader of the Israelite tribal alliance (see R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 175).

verses.zh: 神使恶魔降在亚比米勒和示剑人中间，示剑人就以诡诈待亚比米勒。
verses.en: God sent a spirit to stir up hostility[NOTE:1] between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem. He made the leaders of Shechem disloyal[NOTE:2] to Abimelech.
notes: Heb “an evil spirit.” A nonphysical, spirit being is in view, like the one who volunteered to deceive Ahab (1 Kgs 22:21). The traditional translation, “evil spirit,” implies the being is inherently wicked, perhaps even demonic, but this is not necessarily the case. The Hebrew adjective רָעַה (raʿah) can have a nonethical sense, “harmful; dangerous; calamitous.” When modifying רוּחַ (ruakh, “spirit”) it may simply indicate that the being in view causes harm to the object of God’s judgment. G. F. Moore (Judges [ICC], 253) here refers to a “mischief-making spirit.”
Heb “The leaders of Shechem were disloyal.” The words “he made” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 这是要叫耶路・巴力七十个儿子所受的残害归与他们的哥哥亚比米勒，又叫那流他们血的罪归与帮助他杀弟兄的示剑人。
verses.en: He did this so the violent deaths of Jerub Baal’s 70 sons might be avenged and Abimelech, their half-brother[NOTE:1] who murdered them, might have to pay for their spilled blood, along with the leaders of Shechem who helped him murder them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “their brother.”

Heb “so that the violence done to the 70 sons of Jerub Baal might come, and their blood might be placed on Abimelech, their brother, who murdered them, and upon the leaders of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to murder his brothers.”

verses.zh: 示剑人在山顶上设埋伏，等候亚比米勒。凡从他们那里经过的人，他们就抢夺。有人将这事告诉亚比米勒。
verses.en: The leaders of Shechem rebelled against Abimelech by putting[NOTE:1] bandits in[NOTE:2] the hills, who robbed everyone who traveled by on the road. But Abimelech found out about it.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “set against him bandits.” sn Putting bandits in the hills. This piracy certainly interrupted or discouraged trade, and probably deprived Abimelech of tariffs or tribute. See C. F. Burney, Judges, 277; G. F. Moore, Judges (ICC), 253.
Heb “on the tops of.”
Heb “It was told to Abimelech.”

verses.zh: 以别的儿子迦勒和他的弟兄来到示剑，示剑人都信靠他。
verses.en: Gaal son of Ebed[NOTE:1] came through Shechem with his brothers. The leaders of Shechem transferred their loyalty to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: The name Gaal derives from, or at least sounds like, a Hebrew verb meaning “to abhor, loathe.” His father’s name, Ebed, means “servant.” Perhaps then this could be translated, “loathsome one, son of a servant.” This individual’s very name (which may be the narrator’s nickname for him, not his actual name) seems to hint at his immoral character and lowly social status.

Heb “trusted in him.” Here the verb probably describes more than a mental attitude. It is likely that the Shechemites made an alliance with Gaal and were now trusting him for protection in return for their loyalty (and probably tribute).

verses.zh: 示剑人出城到田间去，摘下葡萄，踹酒，设摆筵宴，进他们神的庙中吃喝，咒诅亚比米勒。
verses.en: They went out to the field, harvested their grapes,[NOTE:1] squeezed out the juice,[NOTE:2] and celebrated. They came to the temple[NOTE:3] of their god and ate, drank, and cursed Abimelech.
notes: Heb “vineyards.”

Heb “stomped” or “trampled.” This refers to the way in which the juice was squeezed out in the wine vats by stepping on the grapes with one’s bare feet. For a discussion of grape harvesting in ancient Israel, see O. Borowski, Agriculture in Iron Age Israel, 110-14.
Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 以别的儿子迦勒说：「亚比米勒是谁？示剑是谁？使我们服事他呢？他不是耶路・巴力的儿子吗？他的帮手不是西布勒吗？你们可以服事示剑的父亲哈抹的后裔。我们为何服事亚比米勒呢？
verses.en: Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerub Baal, and is not Zebul the deputy he appointed?[NOTE:1] Serve the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem! But why should we serve Abimelech?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and Zebul his appointee.”
Heb “him”; the referent (Abimelech) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 惟愿这民归我的手下，我就除掉亚比米勒。」迦勒又对亚比米勒说：「增添你的军兵出来吧。」
verses.en: If only these men[NOTE:1] were under my command,[NOTE:2] I would get rid of Abimelech!” He challenged Abimelech,[NOTE:3] “Muster[NOTE:4] your army and come out for battle!”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “people.”

Heb “in my hand.”sn If only these men were under my command. One might assume from v. 26b that the men were already at his disposal, but perhaps that was not one of the terms of the agreement. Another possibility is that v. 26 is a general summary statement, with vv. 27-29 then detailing how the alliance with Gaal came about.

Heb “said to Abimelech.” On the other hand, the preposition ל (lamed) prefixed to the proper name may be vocative (see R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 178). If so, one could translate, “He boasted, ‘Abimelech….’”
Heb “Make numerous.”
The words “for battle” are interpretive.

verses.zh: 邑宰西布勒听见以别的儿子迦勒的话，就发怒，
verses.en: When Zebul, the city commissioner, heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he was furious.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his anger burned.”

verses.zh: 悄悄地打发人去见亚比米勒，说：「以别的儿子迦勒和他的弟兄到了示剑，煽惑城中的民攻击你。
verses.en: He sent messengers to Abimelech, who was in Arumah,[NOTE:1] reporting, “Beware![NOTE:2] Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers are coming[NOTE:3] to Shechem and inciting the city to rebel against you.[NOTE:4]
notes: The form בְּתָרְמָה (betormah) in the Hebrew text, which occurs only here, has traditionally been understood to mean “secretly” or “with deception.” If this is correct, it is derived from II רָמָה (ramah, “to deceive”). Some interpreters object, pointing out that this would imply Zebul was trying to deceive Abimelech, which is clearly not the case in this context. But this objection is unwarranted. If retained, the phrase would refer instead to deceptive measures used by Zebul to avoid the suspicion of Gaal when he dispatched the messengers from Shechem. The present translation assumes an emendation to “in Arumah” (בָּארוּמָה, baʾrumah), a site mentioned in v. 41 as the headquarters of Abimelech. Confusion of ʾalef and tav in archaic Hebrew script, while uncommon, is certainly not unimaginable.
Heb “Look!”

The participle, as used here, suggests Gaal and his brothers are in the process of arriving, but the preceding verses imply they have already settled in. Perhaps Zebul uses understatement to avoid the appearance of negligence on his part. After all, if he made the situation sound too bad, Abimelech, when he was informed, might ask why he had allowed this rebellion to reach such a stage.

The words “to rebel” are interpretive. The precise meaning of the Hebrew verb צוּר (tsur) is unclear here. It is best to take it in the sense of “to instigate; to incite; to provoke” (see Deut 2:9, 19 and R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 178).

verses.zh: 现在你和跟随你的人今夜起来，在田间埋伏。
verses.en: Now, come up[NOTE:1] at night with your men[NOTE:2] and set an ambush in the field outside the city.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “arise.”
Heb “you and the people who are with you.”
The words “outside the city” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 到早晨太阳一出，你就起来闯城。迦勒和跟随他的人出来攻击你的时候，你便向他们见机而做。」
verses.en: In the morning at sunrise quickly attack the city. When he and his men come out to fight you, do what you can to him.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Look! He and the people who are with him will come out to you, and you will do to him what your hand finds [to do].”

verses.zh: 于是，亚比米勒和跟随他的众人夜间起来，分作四队，埋伏等候示剑人。
verses.en: So Abimelech and all his men came up[NOTE:1] at night and set an ambush outside Shechem; they divided into[NOTE:2] four units.
notes: Heb “and all the people who were with him arose.”
Heb “four heads.” The words “they divided into” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 以别的儿子迦勒出去，站在城门口。亚比米勒和跟随他的人从埋伏之处起来。
verses.en: When Gaal son of Ebed came out and stood at the entrance to the city’s gate, Abimelech and his men got up from their hiding places.

verses.zh: 迦勒看见那些人，就对西布勒说：「看哪，有人从山顶上下来了。」西布勒说：「你看见山的影子，以为是人。」
verses.en: Gaal saw the men[NOTE:1] and said to Zebul, “Look, men are coming down from the tops of the hills.” But Zebul said to him, “You are seeing the shadows on the hills—it just looks like men.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the people” (also in vv. 38, 43, 48). These were warriors, so “men” has been used in the translation, since in ancient Israelite culture soldiers would have been exclusively males.
Heb “the shadow on the hills you are seeing, like men.”

verses.zh: 迦勒又说：「看哪，有人从高处下来，又有一队从米恶尼尼橡树的路上而来。」
verses.en: Gaal again said, “Look, men are coming down from the very center[NOTE:1] of the land. A unit[NOTE:2] is coming by way of the Oak Tree of the Diviners.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “navel.” On the background of the Hebrew expression “the navel of the land,” see R. G. Boling, Judges (AB), 178-79.
Heb “head.”
Some English translations simply transliterated this as a place name (Heb “Elon-meonenim”); cf. NAB, NRSV.

verses.zh: 西布勒对他说：「你曾说，亚比米勒是谁，叫我们服事他？你所夸的口在哪里呢？这不是你所藐视的民吗？你现在出去，与他们交战吧！」
verses.en: Zebul said to him, “Where now are your bragging words,[NOTE:1] ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Are these not the men[NOTE:2] you insulted?[NOTE:3] Go out now and fight them!”
notes: Heb “is your mouth that says.”
Heb “the people.”
Or “despised.”

verses.zh: 于是迦勒率领示剑人出去，与亚比米勒交战。
verses.en: So Gaal led the leaders of Shechem out[NOTE:1] and fought Abimelech.
notes: Heb “So Gaal went out before the leaders of Shechem.”

verses.zh: 亚比米勒追赶迦勒；迦勒在他面前逃跑，有许多受伤仆倒的，直到城门。
verses.en: Abimelech chased him, and Gaal[NOTE:1] ran from him. Many Shechemites[NOTE:2] fell wounded at the entrance of the gate.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Gaal) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The word “Shechemites” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for clarification.

verses.zh: 亚比米勒住在亚鲁玛。西布勒赶出迦勒和他弟兄，不准他们住在示剑。
verses.en: Abimelech went back[NOTE:1] to Arumah; Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “stayed.” Some scholars revise the vowel pointing on this verb from that of the MT, resulting in the translation “and he returned to.” The Lucianic recension of the LXX understands the word in this way.
Heb “drove…out from dwelling in Shechem.”

verses.zh: 次日，民出到田间，有人告诉亚比米勒；
verses.en: The next day the Shechemites[NOTE:1] came out to the field. When Abimelech heard about it,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the people”; the referent (the Shechemites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “And they told Abimelech.”

verses.zh: 他就把他的人分作三队，埋伏在田间，看见示剑人从城里出来，就起来击杀他们。
verses.en: he took his men[NOTE:1] and divided them into three units and set an ambush in the field. When he saw the people coming out of the city,[NOTE:2] he attacked and struck them down.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his people.”
Heb “And he saw and, look, the people were coming out of the city.”
Heb “he arose against them and struck them.”

verses.zh: 亚比米勒和跟随他的一队向前闯去，站在城门口；那两队直闯到田间，击杀了众人。
verses.en: Abimelech and his units[NOTE:1] attacked and blocked[NOTE:2] the entrance to the city’s gate. Two units then attacked all the people in the field and struck them down.
notes: Or possibly, “the unit that was with him.”
Heb “stood [at].”

verses.zh: 亚比米勒整天攻打城，将城夺取，杀了其中的居民，将城拆毁，撒上了盐。
verses.en: Abimelech fought against the city all that day. He captured the city and killed all the people in it. Then he leveled[NOTE:1] the city and spread salt over it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “destroyed.”

Heb “sowed it with salt.”sn The spreading of salt over the city was probably a symbolic act designed to place the site under a curse, deprive it of fertility, and prevent any future habitation. The practice is referred to outside the Bible as well. For example, one of the curses in the Aramaic Sefire treaty states concerning Arpad: “May Hadad sow in them salt and weeds, and may it not be mentioned again!” See J. A. Fitzmyer, The Aramaic Inscriptions of Sefire (BibOr), 15, 53. Deut 29:23, Jer 17:6, and Zeph 2:9 associate salt flats or salty regions with infertility and divine judgment.

verses.zh: 示剑楼的人听见了，就躲入巴力・比利土庙的卫所。
verses.en: When all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem[NOTE:1] heard the news, they went to the stronghold[NOTE:2] of the temple of El Berith.[NOTE:3]
notes: Perhaps the Tower of Shechem was a nearby town, distinct from Shechem proper, or a tower within the city.

Apparently this rare word refers here to the most inaccessible area of the temple, perhaps the inner sanctuary or an underground chamber. It appears only here and in 1 Sam 13:6, where it is paired with “cisterns” and refers to subterranean or cave-like hiding places.
The name El-Berith means “God of the Covenant.” It is probably a reference to the Canaanite high god El.

verses.zh: 有人告诉亚比米勒说：「示剑楼的人都聚在一处。」
verses.en: Abimelech heard[NOTE:1] that all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem were in one place.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and it was told to Abimelech.”
Heb “were assembled.”

verses.zh: 亚比米勒和跟随他的人就都上撒们山。亚比米勒手拿斧子，砍下一根树枝，扛在肩上，对跟随他的人说：「你们看我所行的，也当赶紧照样行。」
verses.en: He and all his men[NOTE:1] went up on Mount Zalmon. He[NOTE:2] took an ax[NOTE:3] in his hand and cut off a tree branch. He put it[NOTE:4] on his shoulder and said to his men, “Quickly, do what you have just seen me do!”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “his people.”
Heb “Abimelech.” The proper name has been replaced with the pronoun (“he”) due to considerations of English style.
The Hebrew text has the plural here.
Heb “he lifted it and put [it].”
Heb “What you have seen me do, quickly do like me.”

verses.zh: 众人就各砍一枝，跟随亚比米勒，把树枝堆在卫所的四围，放火烧了卫所，以致示剑楼的人都死了，男女约有一千。
verses.en: So each of his men also cut off a branch and followed Abimelech. They put the branches[NOTE:1] against the stronghold and set fire to it.[NOTE:2] All the people[NOTE:3] of the Tower of Shechem died—about 1,000 men and women.
notes: The words “the branches” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “they kindled over them the stronghold with fire.”
Or “men,” but the word seems to have a more general sense here, as the conclusion to the sentence suggests.

verses.zh: 亚比米勒到提备斯，向提备斯安营，就攻取了那城。
verses.en: Abimelech moved on[NOTE:1] to Thebez; he besieged and captured it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “went.”
Heb “he camped near Thebez and captured it.”

verses.zh: 城中有一座坚固的楼；城里的众人，无论男女，都逃进楼去，关上门，上了楼顶。
verses.en: There was a fortified[NOTE:1] tower[NOTE:2] in the center of the city, so all the men and women, as well as the city’s leaders, ran into it and locked the entrance. Then they went up to the roof of the tower.
notes: Or “strong.”
Or “fortress.” The same Hebrew term occurs once more in this verse and twice in v. 52.

verses.zh: 亚比米勒到了楼前攻打，挨近楼门，要用火焚烧。
verses.en: Abimelech came and attacked the tower. When he approached the entrance of the tower to set it on fire,

verses.zh: 有一个妇人把一块上磨石抛在亚比米勒的头上，打破了他的脑骨。
verses.en: a woman threw an upper millstone[NOTE:1] down on his[NOTE:2] head and shattered his skull.
notes: A hand mill consisted of an upper stone and larger lower stone. One would turn the upper stone with a handle to grind the grain, which was placed between the stones. An upper millstone, which was typically about two inches thick and a foot or so in diameter, probably weighed 25-30 pounds (11.4-13.6 kg). See G. F. Moore, Judges (ICC), 268; C. F. Burney, Judges, 288.
Heb “Abimelech’s.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun “his” in the translation in keeping with conventions of English narrative style.

verses.zh: 他就急忙喊叫拿他兵器的少年人，对他说：「拔出你的刀来，杀了我吧！免得人议论我说，他为一个妇人所杀。」于是少年人把他刺透，他就死了。
verses.en: He quickly called to the young man who carried his weapons,[NOTE:1] “Draw your sword and kill me, so they will not say,[NOTE:2] ‘A woman killed him.’” So the young man stabbed him and he died.
notes: The Hebrew text adds, “and said to him.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
The Hebrew text adds, “concerning me.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 以色列人见亚比米勒死了，便各回自己的地方去了。
verses.en: When the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, they went home.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “each to his own place.”

verses.zh: 这样，　神报应亚比米勒向他父亲所行的恶，就是杀了弟兄七十个人的恶。
verses.en: God repaid Abimelech for the evil he did to his father by murdering his 70 half brothers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “70 brothers.”

verses.zh: 示剑人的一切恶，　神也都报应在他们头上；耶路・巴力的儿子约坦的咒诅归到他们身上了。
verses.en: God also repaid the men of Shechem for their evil deeds. The curse spoken by Jotham son of Jerub Baal fell[NOTE:1] on them.
notes: Heb “came.”
